item.title: Inspect Any Crack: An Automated End-to-End Crack Segmentation and Severity Assessment Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.14274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Image-based crack analysis is essential for automated infrastructure inspection to reduce the cost, subjectivity, and safety risks of manual surveys. Despite advances in visual crack detection, methods that translate predictions into physically meaningful and engineering-interpretable crack condition information remain limited. To bridge this gap, this study proposes Inspect Any Crack (IAC), an innovative end-to-end crack recognition and condition assessment framework that automatically derives physical geometric measurements and continuous severity scores from concrete-crack imagery. At its core, IAC introduces SACv2-Tiny, an efficient crack segmentation model adapted from a vision foundation model. Trained on the challenging OmniCrack30K dataset, SACv2-Tiny achieved a $62.49\%$ F1-score and $45.45\%$ IoU on the test set and a mean zero-shot F1-score of $69.89\%$ across three unseen datasets, demonstrating robust segmentation that enables downstream analysis with limited post-processing. IAC further processes the predicted masks to quantify physical crack width and affected area using ground-sampling-distance calibration. Validation at 41 caliper-referenced locations yielded a mean relative width error of $7.33\%$. Beyond geometric quantification, IAC introduces a novel continuous crack-condition metric, the Crack Severity Index (CSI), bounded on $[0,100]$, which combines maximum crack width and affected-area ratio into a unified, standards-informed severity measure. Through these developments, IAC advances crack inspection beyond pixel-level recognition toward interpretable and automated infrastructure condition assessment.
item.dc:creator: Ghodsiyeh Rostami, Po-Han Chen, Mahdi S. Hosseini

item.title: Generative AI enables human-centered design of sustainable plant-based foods
item.description: arXiv:2610.15616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dietary transitions away from animal-based meat could reduce food-related environmental burdens, but plant-based alternatives must compete on flavor, texture, and overall liking. Here we extend a generative AI framework with 469 plant-based burger recipes and use it to create six formulations across five primary ingredients: bean, chickpea, lentil, mushroom, and oat. An executive chef translates the AI-generated formulations into standardized preparation protocols and refines the ingredient quantities based on culinary expertise. The integration of generative modeling and culinary expertise defines a human-centered generative AI framework for food design. We evaluate the six burgers in a blinded sensory survey with 101 participants in an operating restaurant and quantify their land use, greenhouse gas emissions, eutrophication potential, and scarcity-weighted water use. We use Big Mac scores from a previous survey as an iconic commercial benchmark. The mushroom burger achieves mean flavor, texture, and overall liking scores similar to the Big Mac, with less than one-third of its estimated environmental impact. The other formulations reduce the estimated impact further, in several cases to near one-tenth of the Big Mac value, but receive lower liking scores. Mixed-effects models quantify associations between sensory attributes and human liking and retain predictive accuracy on independent survey data, with mean absolute errors no greater than 0.52 points on a seven-point scale. Together, these results demonstrate how generative design, culinary expertise, human sensory response, and environmental assessment can converge to create sustainable foods that people want to eat.
item.dc:creator: Vahidullah Tac, Ellen Kuhl

item.title: Koopman Operator Inference for the Chemical Master Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We infer kinetic rates of stochastic reaction networks from molecular-state pairs separated by a fixed time lag, without constructing the large state space of the Chemical Master Equation. Extended dynamic mode decomposition estimates the finite-time evolution of selected functions of the molecular state. A matrix logarithm then gives a projected generator whose species rows determine the rates through the known reaction stoichiometry. A finite set of functions introduces a systematic bias. We construct additional functions from the reaction channels and prove that each level of closure moves the first bias term to higher order. Spectral formulas identify the omitted modes responsible for this bias and show when the logarithm amplifies sampling error. Exact calculations and experiments on five reaction networks confirm the predicted error behavior and show when the added functions improve finite-sample rate recovery.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Dendukuri, Linda Petzold

item.title: An Adjoint Krylov Approach to Parameter Inference for Affine Families of Linear Evolution Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces an adjoint Krylov method for parameter inference in large, sparse linear evolution equations whose system matrices depend affinely on unknown coefficients. We estimate these coefficients from discrete observations by constructing one forward and one adjoint Krylov approximation on each observation interval. Quadrature of the resulting bilinear form gives the full coefficient gradient through sparse matrix-vector products, without evaluating a separate Frechet derivative in every operator direction. We separate the gradient error into forward, adjoint, and quadrature terms and derive residual-based bounds for Markov and Lindblad generators. We also identify cases in which heuristic stopping estimates become small before the gradient has converged. With workspace reuse, we compute library gradients for a 12-qubit Lindblad generator with dimension 1.7 x 10^7 on a single machine with 16 GB of memory. Experiments on chemical master, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky, and Lindblad equations demonstrate accurate gradients and parameter recovery.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Dendukuri, Shivkumar Chandrasekaran, Linda Petzold

item.title: How the Classical Baseline Shapes Machine-Learning Speed Claims in Topology Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.16051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topology optimization places material so that a structure resists deformation under given loads. Machine-learning methods often report large speed-ups over classical, non-learned optimization, but a slow classical code or a less stiff learned design can exaggerate them. We re-ran released code for eight methods on one workstation and studied two in depth: Optimize Any Topology (OAT), a diffusion model that generates designs, and a graph-based neural optimizer. Speeding up only the classical code's finite-element solver cut these two methods' speed-ups by up to 20-fold. We then timed the classical code until its design was at least as stiff as the learned one; for OAT, we read this point off the completed runs. Published timings imply a 134x speed-up for OAT on a 256 x 256 grid; our matched single-design comparisons gave 1.5x to 3.5x. At matched stiffness, the graph-based optimizer was slower than the classical code in all six two-dimensional problems. Of the six other methods, two kept their advantage, one shrank, one reversed and two were not comparable. In an exploratory audit of published claims, language models judged that 8 of 28 speed comparisons in randomly sampled, openly accessible articles lacked evidence of equal design quality; our own review counted 11, so the count depends on who judges. We provide a comparison procedure and a minimum report: classical code, hardware, design quality, what each timing includes, and data-generation and training costs.
item.dc:creator: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

item.title: Towards a Benchmark for Fire Safety Code Interpretation in the Hong Kong AEC Industry
item.description: arXiv:2610.16127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly explored in the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) domain, yet their reliability in regulatory compliance remains uncertain. In this study, we evaluate the performance of LLMs on Hong Kong fire safety codes. In collaboration with domain experts, we create a localized benchmark dataset comprising both multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and open-ended questions (OEQs) to evaluate 12 widely used proprietary and open-source models. Our findings show that top-performing proprietary models achieve 80-90% accuracy on MCQs, whereas open-source models generally lag behind. However, on open-ended evaluation, expert human assessments reveal an accuracy range of only 50-70%, demonstrating that LLMs still have substantial room for improvement in specialized compliance tasks.
item.dc:creator: Le Qiu, Zhuan Anne Zhang, Hok Ming Adeline Chan, Emmanuele Chersoni

item.title: Rigid Bodies as Accidental Seismoscopes: Exact Time Stepper Inversion and an Estimate of Ground Acceleration in the 2026 La Guaira Earthquake
item.description: arXiv:2610.16912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An unknown ground excitation is recovered from the measured response of a rigid body sliding in two dimensions on an inclined surface under Coulomb friction, a system with no classical solution, whose sampled trajectories come from a time stepper. The Moreau stepper is shown to admit an exact inverse, explicit, non-iterative and vectorizable, giving the ground acceleration over each step in closed form, without regularization or an assumed source model. The inverse evaluates the friction direction at the end of the step, not its beginning. Inverting the continuous equation instead is not a secondary discretization choice: the two inverses differ by an exact identity proportional to the rotation of the sliding direction within the step, bounded by twice the frictional deceleration, which is of order one g for typical interfaces. The identity is inactive in one dimension, which explains why the sliding block literature has not confronted it. Verification against a manufactured reference solution recovers it to machine precision. On the field record, the discrepancy reaches 0.10g in root mean square, which exceeds the whole propagated uncertainty of the reported peak, and it suppresses 17% of the recovered travel, behaving as a bias, not noise, so root-mean-square agreement in acceleration understates it. The method is applied to surveillance video of a delineator post that slid in the 24 June 2026 La Guaira earthquake, yielding a peak ground acceleration of 0.912 +/- 0.047g, and a lower bound of 0.47g independent of the imagery. Displaced rigid bodies can therefore provide quantitative ground-motion information where instruments are absent.
item.dc:creator: Rafael Ruiz, Ruben Boroschek, Eduardo Nu\~nez

item.title: Multi-Objective Amortized CDRH3 Sequence Sampling Diversifies Promising Antibody Candidates
item.description: arXiv:2610.16920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Antibody therapeutics have transformed treatment across diverse therapeutic areas and have become central to modern medicine. While recent machine learning approaches aim to accelerate antibody discovery through structure-based design and target-affinity optimization, successful candidates must also satisfy broad developability constraints, including structural compatibility, low immunogenicity, and favorable biophysical properties, while remaining sufficiently diverse to provide sufficient coverage of design space to mitigate later-stage development failures. We introduce a preference-conditioned multi-objective generative flow network (GFN) fine-tuning pipeline for fixed-framework CDRH3 loop redesign that fine-tunes a biological sequence model against many inexpensive proxies covering backbone compatibility, sequence likelihood, immunogenicity risk, novelty, and developability liabilities. It combines up to fourteen predictive rewards in a single policy trained to sample CDRH3 loops across 623 SAbDab antibody structures, leveraging a reward reduction strategy to preserve Pareto dominance under this learned map. We also introduce a novel autoregressive span-in-filling variant of AMPLIFY-350M that serves both as a scaffold-conditioned CDRH3 generation prior and as a direct conditional likelihood scorer. We evaluated reward scores, diversity, and design quality on loops sampled on 45 held-out antibody complexes to assess structural consistency, confidence, aggregation propensity, stability, and antigen binding. Compared with the inverse-folding methods ProteinMPNN and ESM-IF, our approach produces roughly 10x more distinct acceptable candidates per design at 50% sequence identity, while holding 10% of the 14-objective Pareto front pooled across methods, trading per-sample quality for greater exploration of novel possible structures.
item.dc:creator: Joseph D. Viviano, Almer van der Sloot, Quentin Fournier, Robert M. Vernon, Christopher James Langmead, Yoshua Bengio

item.title: PROTEAN: Beyond De Novo Generation - Can LLM Agents Perform Text-Guided Protein Structure Editing?
item.description: arXiv:2610.17765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI has achieved remarkable success in de novo protein design, yet protein engineering typically begins with existing, characterized proteins. The primary demand is targeted local editing, e.g., engineering a specific region to optimize affinity, alter immunogenicity, or improve stability, while strictly preserving core catalytic motifs and overall scaffold integrity. However, no standardized framework currently exists for carrying out and evaluating such edits. In current generative-design workflows, researchers often need to manually specify complex low-level parameters and rely on repetitive, trial-and-error sampling and evaluation across generative backends to search for viable conformations. While large language models (LLMs) offer an intuitive interface to express these goals using natural language, prevailing structure-generation models cannot directly interpret high-level human instructions. To bridge this gap, we introduce PROTEAN, a standardized benchmark for text-guided protein structural editing. PROTEAN comprises 380 sub-tasks spanning six intervention families and evaluates a two-stage pipeline in which an LLM translates natural-language goals into backend-specific geometric constraints and a generative model remodels the protein backbone. A two-tier evaluation separates geometric compliance, including target attainment and off-target scope fidelity, from biophysical realizability assessed by inverse folding and refolding consistency. Across five frontier LLMs paired with three backends, strict end-to-end biophysical success starts at just 7.0%. Ablation studies show that LLM constraint compilation is already highly accurate, whereas the main bottlenecks are backend-specific scope leakage and refolding failure. PROTEAN provides an open testbed for developing autonomous, multi-backend macromolecular design agents.
item.dc:creator: Encheng Su, Xinping Liu, Yizhou Wang, Bozitao Zhong, Pengze Li, Jianyu Wu, Mingxiao Li, Xinzhu Ma, Aoran Wang, Liang Hong, Wanli Ouyang, Chen Tang, Houqiang Li, Shixiang Tang

item.title: Multi-Agent Path Planning via Compatible Encounter-Space Allocation in Crowded Spaces Dynamically Occupied by Work Activities
item.description: arXiv:2610.17912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lifelong multiagent path planning on construction floors must accommodate continually changing goals and work occupancy. Existing planners can update paths and timing online, but work motion space coupling changes the spatial basis of unfinished encounters, while rerouting affects later encounters. Planning must therefore construct and maintain local encounter possibility. We propose Width based Planning with Compatible Encounter Space Allocation (WP), which constructs shared passage relationships from actual encounter demands and real time widths. Shared channels, ordered anchors, and urgency based updates coordinate successive encounters while retaining individual greedy motion between them. A necessary and sufficient width condition for fixed-point position exchange and a necessary directional condition for composite exchange provide geometric grounds for channel construction and encounter relocation. In crowded floor computational experiments, WP maintained route continuation after occupancy changes and enabled multi agent clearing, with infrequent, brief near stops. Complete run comparisons with four methods showed 25.2% to 52.2% more mean goal arrivals than the best baseline at each configuration of 5 to 10 agents, with lower mean computation time than the rolling horizon K_CBS adaptation. The contribution is a planning principle that constructs and continuously maintains local passage relationships from real time space, unifying shared spatial allocation and conditional local clearing to extend lifelong planning to work motion space coupling.
item.dc:creator: Boda Liu, Xuezhi Yang, Bin Yang, Shu Li

item.title: FleetGuard:Identity-Capped Conformal Risk Allocation for Reliable UAV Edge-Cloud Offloading
item.description: arXiv:2610.18003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compromised UAV reporters can poison latency telemetry and attract offloaded tasks to degraded servers. We present FleetGuard, an identity-capped conformal offloader for local, edge, and cloud execution. With equal buffers of m scores and a cap of K compromised identities, a Km rank correction retains one-sided fixed-level coverage without an honest-reporter majority. A deterministic repair scheduler allocates task-specific risk under fleet, capacity, and deadline constraints. Heavy-tailed simulations with eight reporters, four edges, 30 independent seeds, and 20 batches per seed and condition yield 2.08% deadline misses under seven low-score compromised reporters (95% clustered interval: 1.94-2.24%), compared with approximately 9.6% for pooled conformal, reporter-median, and mean rules. FleetGuard saves 22.3% energy over fixed-risk BRC and approaches adaptive exact assignment within 1.1%, with 2.6x lower mean scheduling time.
item.dc:creator: Junhao Wei, Haochen Li, Yifu Zhao, Yanxiao Li, Dexing Yao, Baili Lu, Ngai Cheong, Sio-Kei Im, Xu Yang, Yapeng Wang

item.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning in Oncology
item.description: arXiv:2610.18682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning has enabled substantial advances in oncology, including cancer detection and diagnosis, medical image analysis, tumor characterization, treatment planning, response assessment, and outcome prediction. However, conventional data-driven models often require large annotated datasets, exhibit limited generalization across heterogeneous clinical settings, and lack explicit mechanisms for incorporating the physical, physiological, and biological principles underlying cancer development and treatment. Physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) integrates governing physical laws, mechanistic models, physiological constraints, and domain knowledge into deep learning frameworks, providing a principled approach for learning from sparse, noisy, and heterogeneous oncological data. This review presents a task-oriented synthesis of PIDL methods across oncology, encompassing neural networks, Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, convolutional and vision architectures, neural operators, generative models, and hybrid physics-data-driven frameworks. Their applications are examined across cancer detection and diagnosis, image reconstruction and analysis, tumor characterization, quantitative imaging, tumor progression, treatment response, radiation therapy, treatment planning, and multimodal clinical modeling. Based on the synthesized methodological and application-level evidence, we develop task-optimized PIDL workflows that align the clinical task with appropriate data representations, physical constraints, model architectures, and validation strategies. We further analyze key challenges, including physical-model fidelity, computational scalability, uncertainty quantification, domain generalization, standardized benchmarking, and clinical validation.
item.dc:creator: Scindhiya Laxmi, Vivek S. Yadav, Ameya D. Jagtap

item.title: Generalized PINN-Based Inverse Estimation of Spatially Varying Heat Transfer Coefficients with Transfer Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.14008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study investigates generalized boundary representations and transfer learning for physics-informed neural-network (PINN) estimation of spatially varying convective heat transfer coefficients (HTCs) in jet impingement cooling. Piecewise-linear (PWL) and neural-network boundary estimators are inferred from transient interior-temperature measurements and evaluated against CFD-CHT reference HTC profiles at Reynolds numbers of 5000, 10000 and 15000. A discrete Adjoint-FEM formulation with gradient regularization based on the $H^1$-seminorm provides an independent inverse-method comparison. Transfer learning is investigated under two source-target conditions: transfer between noise levels at the same Reynolds number, and transfer from a controlled Gaussian-profile problem to CFD-CHT-derived target problems at different Reynolds numbers. For the representative Re = 5000 target with 5% measurement noise, quadratic, PWL, and neural-network PINNs achieve relative HTC-profile errors of 5.08, 5.31 and 5.19%, respectively, while generalized representations reduce the error for the Re = 15000 target from 16.76% for the quadratic PINN to 14.41% and 14.46%. Transfer learning reduces target-training time by 57.86-81.71% for fixed-Reynolds-number transfer and by 50.59-84.94% for Gaussian-to-CHT transfer. Its effect on reconstruction accuracy is target dependent: fixed-profile PWL transfer remains within 0.30 percentage points of scratch training, whereas Gaussian-to-CHT transfer produces differences of 0.10-1.52 percentage points across targets and representations. These results demonstrate that generalized PINN representations can accommodate spatially varying HTC profiles without a prescribed quadratic form, while transfer learning can substantially reduce target-training cost for repeated inverse estimation, with the resulting reconstruction accuracy depending on source-target compatibility.
item.dc:creator: Pradipan Maitra, Jariful Hassan, Arijit Hazra

item.title: SAGE: Efficient Protected Vision-Language Inference on Smart Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2610.14089v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Smart glasses are a promising platform for vision-language assistants, but private split inference remains expensive: protecting visual representations before transmission does not remove the cost of on-device vision encoding, wide protected tokens, or hardware-unaware execution. We present SAGE (Smart-glasses-Aware Guarded Encoding), a hardware-aware framework for efficient protected VLM inference on smart glasses. SAGE keeps raw images and unprotected visual tokens on the trusted device, reduces visual input cost, executes shape-specialized INT8 graphs, and compresses protected representations into compact 256-dimensional INT8 packets before transmission. Unlike efficiency methods optimized only for nominal model size, SAGE selects its operating point using downstream answer quality together with measured latency, memory, and thermal behavior on real Mentra Live glasses. On a matched Qwen workload, SAGE reduces glasses inference latency by 39.18%, device-sensor temperature rise by 21.91%, and protected packet size by 96.56%, while retaining 85.62% of the protected reference's relaxed utility and comparable prompted containment. Direct glasses-to-phone tests deliver all 192 packets and reduce median packet-plus-acknowledgment time from 71.3 to 10.0 ms. The compact protected interface also transfers across four additional VLM families. These results show that private wearable VLM inference must be optimized jointly across representation protection, communication, and real-device execution rather than through model compression alone.
item.dc:creator: Zhimin Li, Pan Wang, Jingxian Chen, Yuantao Tang, Qian Lou, Jingtong Hu

item.title: Coarse-Graining Recursive Expert Computation: Continuation-Relative Interfaces and Failure Modes
item.description: arXiv:2610.14413v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational coarse-graining aims to replace a sequence of updates with a cheaper module while preserving task performance. We present a continuation-relative evaluation framework that assesses replacements through the computation that follows them, using downstream task quality and total execution cost as joint criteria. The framework distinguishes boundary representations, summaries of skipped computation, executed operations, and downstream loss. It makes interfaces and permitted deployment information explicit, combines fine-path references with directly trained controls using the same shortened architecture, and accounts for selection overhead. An exact loss decomposition separates replacement effects at a fixed downstream action from effects of changing that action. A finite construction shows how retained information can reduce the stipulated cost of zero-error prediction under fixed information and controller restrictions. Experiments in two frozen pretrained language models show that representation fidelity and task loss can favor different fitting objectives. In a prespecified comparison on a 1.7-billion-parameter model, next-token-loss training lowers in-distribution negative log-likelihood by 0.1901 nats per scored token compared with reconstructing the skipped blocks' output, using the same optimizer and update count. This ranking reverses in all nine paired comparisons under distribution shift. In a recursive expert prototype, the jointly adapted candidate lowers task error relative to frozen-bank and router-only baselines, but trails directly trained controls, and the tested input-only selectors fail the joint quality-cost criteria. Together, the protocol and studies provide explicit criteria and diagnostics for distinguishing useful computational replacement from local approximation gains within specified interfaces and evaluation settings.
item.dc:creator: Shihua Yu, Yanzhi Wang, Tianchi Chen

item.title: Automatic assembly modeling through attention-based assembly feature mate prediction and assembly feature pattern recognition
item.description: arXiv:2610.14633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Assembly modeling plays an important role in constructing product models, yet it is still mainly performed via interactive operations that are experience-dependent and labor-intensive. Data-driven strategies hold promise for automating this process; however, existing approaches either predict poses that cannot directly generate editable B-Rep assembly constraints or require prescribed part pairs or predefined assembly faces. To reduce the large candidate space of constraint prediction without predefined assembly faces, we propose a data-driven framework based on assembly feature mate prediction. The framework performs automatic assembly modeling from unassembled B-Rep parts, using assembly features to group the geometric entities of local mating interfaces and restrict candidate formation. Given the lack of suitable assembly feature annotations in existing datasets, we construct a large-scale dataset through an automatic annotation pipeline. Using the annotated dataset, we train an attention-based network to predict assembly feature mates, with Engineering Compatibility Fusion (ECF) incorporating explicit engineering compatibility into learned matching scores. To improve the accuracy of automatic assembly modeling, we use assembly feature patterns (AFPs) to guide the matching process. Finally, a post-processing search selects assembly feature mate and AFP mate candidates, whose associated constraints are generated and solved to complete assembly modeling. Experimental results show that the framework achieves assembly constraint accuracies of 74.79% on the six-assembly comparison set and 64.09% on the extended test set of 16 assemblies, which includes the comparison set. With ground-truth face labels supplied as additional input, the corresponding accuracies increase to 81.78% and 80.93%, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Ziheng Dai, Wanbin Pan, Zhihong Tang, Shuming Gao

item.title: Are implicit schemes needed in adaptive time stepping for PDEs?
item.description: arXiv:2610.14884v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Implicit time integration is the standard way to overcome the tight CFL time step restriction when solving nonstationary PDEs numerically. However, within an adaptive time accurate integration, the time step size selection is governed not only by stability but also by accuracy requirements. Therefore, an eligible question to ask is: is (unconditionally) stable implicit time stepping really needed if the time step is restricted by accuracy considerations anyway? And how much do we then lose (in terms of the time step size) when switching from the expensive implicit time stepping to stabilized explicit schemes? An answer to this question is also important because such a switch is often done when solving large scale nonstationary PDEs on massively parallel computers. This paper attempts to answer these questions by numerical tests for two particular adaptive time accurate settings: (i)~nonstationary convection-diffusion equations and (ii)~nonlinear heat equations.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail A. Botchev

item.title: A single LU~factorization approach to model reduction for linear system families with a quadratic matrix pencil
item.description: arXiv:2610.14902v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: To solve a family of large linear systems where the system matrix depends on the family parameter quadratically, we propose a new solution approach. Our method employs the derivatives of solutions with respect to the parameter. It turns out that the accumulated solution derivatives of increasing order, evaluated at a single specially chosen parameter value, provide successively better approximations to solution subspaces for the whole linear system family. We show that the derivatives can be computed by a recurrence, involving, at each step, solving a linear system with the same matrix. Constructing an orthonormal basis for the subspace spanned by the derivatives then leads to an efficient solver where just a single (sparse) LU factorization (or a single preconditioner setup in an iterative scheme) suffices to solve the whole linear system family. We call the new method ODB (orthonormal derivative basis method). As shown in numerical tests, compared to conventional solution methods, the ODB method allows to drastically reduce computational costs.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail A. Botchev, Leonid Knizhnerman, Nikolai L. Zamarashkin, Dmitry A. Zheltkov

item.title: Use Of Convolutional Neural Networks In Detection Of Branch Dieback Disease In Pequi Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.15049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study aims to evaluate and compare convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, specifically AlexNet, Inception, LeNet, VGG16, and MobileNet, for diagnosing branch dieback (seca-dos-ponteiros) in pequi trees (Caryocar brasiliense). This disease represents a severe threat to tree development and fruit yield, causing substantial economic and ecological losses. The methodology implements computer vision techniques using Python libraries, including Scikit-learn, NumPy, TensorFlow, and Matplotlib, to process and evaluate visual data. The CNN models analyze images of leaves, branches, and flower spikes to detect pathological patterns, such as alterations in texture and coloration. Ultimately, this comparative analysis identifies the most effective architecture for accurately distinguishing healthy plants from diseased ones.
item.dc:creator: Ronilson Rodrigues Pinho, Elua Ramos Coutinho, Nilza de Lima Pereira Sales, Sildenir Aalves Ribeiro, Sergio Manuel Serra da Cruz

item.title: Dissipative Lagrangian Neural Networks for the Interpretable Modelling of Passive Mechanical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.15996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose the Dissipative Lagrangian Neural Network (dLNN), a continuous-time system identification technique that separately learns the conservative and dissipative dynamics of a mechanical system directly from data. A key contribution is a novel parametrisation of dissipative forces that (i) is structurally constrained to be dissipative, enforcing passivity of the learned model, (ii) cannot absorb conservative mechanics, and (iii) retains sufficient expressivity to represent a broad family of state-dependent damping and regularised friction forces. The model is validated on prediction tasks on two real-world mechanical systems: trajectory prediction of a chaotic double pendulum and inverse-dynamics modelling of a six-degree-of-freedom industrial robot. Across these tasks, the dLNN demonstrates improved predictive performance over existing Lagrangian architectures while remaining competitive with a black-box neural model. The imposed physical structure also improves generalisation to unseen states, with the benefits becoming particularly pronounced when training data is limited. Finally, we introduce a symbolic distillation procedure that extracts closed-form expressions from the learned physical components. Applied to the industrial robot, this produces interpretable symbolic models that retain high predictive accuracy while reducing the computational overhead associated with evaluating neural Lagrangian models.
item.dc:creator: Rob Seabourne, Alice Cicirello

item.title: Constructed regional photovoltaic generation fields improve ultra-short-term distributed solar forecasting
item.description: arXiv:2610.16110v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ultra-short-term forecasting of densely distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems remains challenging because external meteorological and satellite products may not adequately resolve rapid local variations, while heterogeneous PV systems exhibit different generation responses under similar atmospheric conditions. Meanwhile, dense PV fleets provide spatially distributed measurements that reveal regional generation dynamics. Here, we reformulate fleet-level PV forecasting from modeling discrete station time series to predicting explicit, spatially structured regional PV generation fields. We develop SatPV-Field, a regional-to-local forecasting framework that transforms distributed PV measurements into image-like generation fields and models their spatiotemporal evolution. By combining historical PV fields with satellite-derived future shortwave radiation guidance and meteorological forecasts, the framework predicts future regional generation states, which subsequently provide location-specific guidance for individual-station forecasting. Experiments involving 496 distributed PV systems, including 446 source stations and 50 held-out target stations, demonstrate that these regional fields can be effectively forecast and used to improve station-level predictions. The proposed approach reduces station-level MAE by approximately 10.0% relative to the best-performing single-station temporal baseline and by 2.5% relative to a graph-based regional forecasting approach using the same source fleet. These findings establish an explicit spatial-field modeling paradigm that connects regional generation dynamics with individual-site forecasting.
item.dc:creator: Dayin Chen, Xiaodan Shi, Xin Xu, Zhongyue Su, Shibo Zhu, Dongxiao Zhang, Yuntian Chen, Jinyue Yan

item.title: Interactive 4D Volumetric Liquid Forecasting under Moving-Solid Interaction
item.description: arXiv:2610.16167v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose the task of Interactive 4D Volumetric Liquid Forecasting: predicting the spatiotemporal evolution of a future dense 3D liquid velocity field conditioned on how a solid object moves through it. This task provides an upstream physical forecasting primitive for systems that need to reason about motion-conditioned liquid response, including robotic liquid manipulation, digital twins, and rigid-fluid video generation. Existing works have made efforts in predicting flow around static or prescribed solid geometries and synthesizing visually plausible fluid motion. Yet these approaches provide limited coverage for interactive liquid dynamics, as they are not capable of forecasting how a moving solid induces a future full-domain liquid response. In this forecasting scenario, the hydrodynamic effect is condensed near an evolving liquid-solid interface, but the prediction target is a global spatiotemporal rollout. To address this challenge, we propose a two-level recurrent forecasting framework, TIDE/TIDES: TIDE isolates localized interface-driven forecasting, while TIDES adds transport-aware coupling and explicit stabilization to reduce accumulated rollout error. Across adapted neighboring baselines, controlled component ablations, motion/size OOD tests, and long-horizon evaluation, TIDES achieves the best forecasting performance and the ablations identify localized interaction, transport coupling, and stabilization as the key contributors. Together, our task formulation, benchmark, and TIDE/TIDES study establish a controlled foundation for moving-solid-conditioned dense liquid forecasting. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/jongwonryu/TIDE-TIDES.
item.dc:creator: Jongwon Ryu, Sunjae Yoon, Junyeong Kim

item.title: AeroChem: Closed-loop Physics-Informed State Space Modeling for Long-term Chemically-Reactive Air Quality Forecasting--Extended Version
item.description: arXiv:2610.16630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate long-term air quality forecasting is challenging due to long-range transport, meteorological variability, and nonlinear chemical reactions underlying secondary pollutant formation. Purely data-driven models often suffer from long-horizon drift and lack physical consistency, while existing physics-informed approaches commonly follow open-loop designs that fuse neural and physical components only at the output level. We propose AeroChem, a closed-loop physics-informed state space framework for chemically reactive air quality forecasting. AeroChem adopts a two-branch co-correction design: a UDE-based process branch provides a structured but imperfect physical prior, while a Mamba-based virtual measurement branch captures long-range temporal context and produces probabilistic virtual observations. Neural Kalman Fusion couples the two branches by correcting the latent physical state at each forecasting step and feeding the posterior state back into the simulator, reducing long-horizon drift. We further introduce HanoiAir, a real-world dataset integrating pollutant concentrations, meteorology, and emission inventories. Experiments on HanoiAir and a public benchmark show that AeroChem improves long-horizon stability and sudden-change forecasting.
item.dc:creator: Kien Le Trung, Tung Kieu, Dinh Duc Nha Nguyen, Cuong Do, Bin Yang, Phi Long Nguyen

item.title: Learning Incompressible 3D Flows from Sparse Samples: A Set Transformer Approach to Divergence-Free Kernel Fitting
item.description: arXiv:2610.16645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recovering divergence-free velocity fields from sparse and corrupted observations requires reconciling physical consistency, expressive representations, and robustness to missing data. We introduce DFK-Former, a set-to-field transformer that reconstructs divergence-free velocity fields from sparse, noisy, and irregularly sampled 3D observations. The model is inherently invariant to the number and ordering of input samples and predicts the parameters of a divergence-free kernel representation, producing continuous, mesh-free velocity fields that satisfy incompressibility exactly by construction rather than approximately through soft constraints or projection operators. Unlike existing divergence-free kernel approaches, which estimate kernel coefficients via a separate optimization for each field, DFK-Former predicts these coefficients directly in a single forward pass. This eliminates costly iterative fitting while providing a learned prior that enables accurate reconstruction even when observations are insufficient to uniquely determine the field. To enhance representational power, we introduce adaptive and anisotropic divergence-free kernels that preserve exact incompressibility guarantees while capturing more complex flow structures. Extensive experiments across varying levels of sparsity, noise, and occlusion, including transfer to real Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) turbulence data, demonstrate substantial gains in both accuracy and efficiency. DFK-Former reduces endpoint error by up to 4.6x compared to per-field divergence-free-kernel optimization, while reconstructing each field in 7.5 ms instead of 9.8 s, yielding a speedup of more than three orders of magnitude. These results establish direct, feed-forward prediction of divergence-free kernel parameters as a practical and effective paradigm for physically consistent velocity-field reconstruction from sparse observations.
item.dc:creator: Ramzi Idoughi, Radouan Boukharfane, Peter Wonka

item.title: Tracing Money Flows in the Multi-Token Cryptocurrency Network
item.description: arXiv:2610.16981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tracing money flows in cryptocurrency transaction networks is challenging because funds can move across accounts, transactions, and token layers. We propose a transaction-aware graph in which nodes represent account--asset states within transactions, while edges encode observed transfers, inferred asset transformations, and temporal inter-transaction sequences. Applied to Aave borrow--repay flows, we compare graph construction and edge-pruning strategies and extract shortest paths using a heuristic weighting. Our results reveal a trade-off between reachability and interpretability and uncover frequent token sequences underlying how borrowed assets are transformed before repayment. This work lays a foundation for general, interpretable multi-token flow tracing.
item.dc:creator: Natkamon Tovanich, C\'{e}lestin Coquid\'{e}

item.title: Delegating Earth science model calibration to knowledge-guided LLM agents
item.description: arXiv:2610.18378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Applying process-based Earth science models to new sites and questions often requires expert calibration decisions. Reliable delegation to language-model agents must preserve scientific competence and reproducibility. Here we develop a general calibration harness (GCH) for end-to-end delegation from a calibration request to assessed results. Constrained by a knowledge infrastructure (KI) and a validation convention, agents define parameter domains, observation mappings and objectives, and generate model-specific code. GCH checks the formulations against the same declarations and freezes them before numerical search and assessment, which require no further agent judgement. Agent-authored workflows executed across six model families, with assessment identifying unmet criteria. In snow-model tests, five of five knowledge-guided specifications executed on the first attempt, compared with none of five given only the model name, achieving validation Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.81-0.94 against 0.57 for defaults. Under a common objective, independent GR4J formulations yielded scores within 0.001 NSE; re-evaluating eleven saved parameter vectors reproduced their metrics. In ten paired VIC tests with matched budgets, fixed search was non-inferior to continuing agent proposals (margin, -0.02 NSE; median difference, -0.003). This separation enables end-to-end calibration delegation with inspectable scientific choices and reproducible numerical evaluation.
item.dc:creator: Zhanliang Zhu, Ziwei Li, Liujun Zhu, Yuchen Liu, Junliang Jin, Jianyun Zhang

item.title: Implementation and Security Analysis of Cryptocurrencies Based on Ethereum
item.description: arXiv:2504.21367v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Blockchain technology has set off a wave of decentralization in the world since its birth. The trust system constructed by blockchain technology based on cryptography algorithm and computing power provides a practical and powerful solution to solve the trust problem in human society. In order to make more convenient use of the characteristics of blockchain and build applications on it, smart contracts appear. By defining some trigger automatic execution contracts, the application space of blockchain is expanded and the foundation for the rapid development of blockchain is laid. This is blockchain 2.0. However, the programmability of smart contracts also introduces vulnerabilities. In order to cope with the insufficient security guarantee of high-value application networks running on blockchain 2.0 and smart contracts, this article will be represented by Ethereum to introduce the technical details of understanding blockchain 2.0 and the operation principle of contract virtual machines, and explain how cryptocurrencies based on blockchain 2.0 are constructed and operated. The common security problems and solutions are also discussed. Based on relevant research and on-chain practice, this paper provides a complete and comprehensive perspective to understanding cryptocurrency technology based on blockchain 2.0 and provides a reference for building more secure cryptocurrency contracts.
item.dc:creator: Pengfei Gao, Dechao Kong, Xiaoqi Li

item.title: A bifidelity sparse-grid surrogate model driven by a discrepancy indicator
item.description: arXiv:2511.20187v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sparse-grid approximations based on Lagrange polynomials are one of the staple methods for approximating functions that are high-dimensional and expensive to evaluate, e.g. in the context of PDE-based parametric design exploration. They are, however, known to have limited granularity: refining these sparse-grid approximations may require multiple additional function evaluations, potentially leading to computational inefficiency. To address this issue, we propose a selection criterion for the candidate collocation points introduced by the refinement procedure: the function is evaluated only at those points for which a suitable (and crucially zero-cost) discrepancy indicator suggests that the additional evaluation would significantly change the resulting approximation. The remaining collocation points are instead assigned values predicted by the already available sparse-grid approximation, i.e., following a bifidelity approach that reduces costs while preserving accuracy. The effectiveness of this methodology is demonstrated on several benchmark functions and on an engineering application concerning flashback phenomena in hydrogen-fueled perforated burners.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Rosellini, Filippo Fruzza, Alessandro Mariotti, Maria Vittoria Salvetti, Lorenzo Tamellini

item.title: Nonparametric Stochastic Subspaces via the Bootstrap Method for Characterizing Model Error
item.description: arXiv:2512.15624v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reliable forward uncertainty quantification in engineering requires methods that account for aleatory and epistemic uncertainties. In many applications, epistemic effects arising from uncertain parameters and model form dominate prediction error and strongly influence engineering decisions. Because distinguishing and representing each source separately is often infeasible, their combined effect is typically analyzed using a unified model-error framework. Model error directly affects model credibility and predictive reliability; yet its characterization remains challenging. To address this need, we introduce a bootstrap-based stochastic subspace model for characterizing model error in the stochastic reduced-order modeling framework. Given a snapshot matrix of state vectors, the method leverages the empirical data distribution to induce a sampling distribution over principal subspaces for reduced order modeling. The resulting stochastic model enables improved characterization of model error in computational mechanics compared with existing approaches. The method offers several advantages: (1) it is assumption-free and leverages the empirical data distribution; (2) it enforces linear constraints (such as boundary conditions) by construction; (3) it requires only one hyperparameter, significantly simplifying the training process; and (4) its algorithm is straightforward to implement. We evaluate the method's performance against existing approaches using numerical examples in computational mechanics and structural dynamics.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: ASCE-ASME J. Risk Uncertainty Eng. Syst., Part A: Civ. Eng. 12(4), 04026061 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Akash Yadav, Ruda Zhang

item.title: Cosm: orchestrated collective dynamics give rise to rapid computational search at the solution frontier
item.description: arXiv:2605.30355v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce Collective Switched Motion (Cosm), a heuristic optimization framework based on orchestrated collective dynamics. Cosm organizes the objective into conflict-minimized subobjectives and activates them sequentially, temporally separating competing local influences. The interplay of switching and local interactions among variables, supplemented by structured correlated perturbations, gives rise to collective search behavior including coordinated cluster motion. Using this framework, we develop and test a solver for sparse Ising optimization. On G64, a large sparse instance with a highly heterogeneous degree distribution from the longstanding Gset Max-Cut benchmark suite, Cosm establishes a new best-known cut of 8753. On large random-graph instances G61 and G70, whose best-known cuts of 5799 and 9595 have been difficult for prior heuristics to attain, a vectorized CPU implementation of Cosm reliably reaches these cuts with times-to-target of 15 s and 2.4 s, respectively. Cosm also heuristically attains the certified optimum of G81, the largest Gset instance (a 20,000-variable two-dimensional spin glass), along with those of G72 and G77. Tests on planted-solution spin-glass benchmarks suggest more favorable empirical scaling than that previously reported for seven compared solvers. Cosm demonstrates that, from simple interacting elements and a new form of orchestration, effective search can emerge.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth M. Zick, Nikhil Shukla, Alexander Marakov

item.title: Non-linear mechanical field reconstruction coupling recurrent neural networks with physics-informed graph neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2606.10909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reconstructing local stress fields in heterogeneous microstructures under non-linear, history-dependent loading remains a major computational bottleneck in multi-scale simulations. We propose a coupled LSTM-GNN framework that links the temporal and spatial aspects of local stress field reconstruction. A Long Short-Term Memory network encodes macroscopic stress-strain sequences into a compact hidden state that captures the path-dependent constitutive response, while a physics-informed Graph Neural Network reconstructs the spatially-resolved stress field at each time step. We introduce a relative weighting strategy with linear warm-up to balance the data-driven reconstruction loss and a discrete divergence-based equilibrium penalty. This resolves the scale mismatch that prevents fixed-weight formulations from converging in the elasto-plastic regime. The model is trained on 10,000 non-proportional loading paths applied to a periodic plate-with-a-hole microstructure and von Mises elasto-plasticity. The model achieves three orders of magnitude speedup over finite element simulations and generalizes to loading sequences twice the training length, with 1.9% cumulative error. Because the graph relies on mesh connectivity instead of the specific element type, one trained surrogate can be applied directly without retraining to meshes with different element types and to both coarser and finer resolutions, while in all cases reproducing the high-fidelity quad-element FE field used during training. Indeed, the message passing characteristics inherent to GNN and MeshGraphNet architecture render the model mesh-agnostic. Analysis of the LSTM hidden states suggests a low-dimensional structure related to the internal state variables of the constitutive model.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Ricardo Guevara Garban, Yves Chemisky, \'Etienne Pruli\`ere, Micha\"el Cl\'ement, Martin Abendroth, Bj\"orn Kiefer

item.title: FinRankGRPO: Optimizing LLMs for Listwise Financial Asset Ranking via Group Relative Policy Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2609.24175v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at understanding unstructured financial contexts, their direct use in portfolio optimization is limited by a mismatch between next-token prediction and the listwise ranking objectives required for asset allocation. They also struggle with precise numerical forecasting, leading to instability and arithmetic hallucinations. To bridge this gap, we propose FinRankGRPO, a framework that shifts LLM based portfolio construction from direct numerical prediction to listwise ranking of financial assets. We introduce a two-stage training process, supervised finetuning on Chain-of-Thought reasoning data, followed by our Financial Asset Ranking via Group Relative Policy Optimization with a Spearman rank correlation reward that aligns generated asset rankings with ground truth market orderings. The second stage uses a novel Spearman rank correlation reward to explicitly align the model's generative preferences with ground truth market orderings. Experimental results show that FinRankGRPO outperforms traditional quantitative and state-of-the-art commercial models, achieving a Sharpe ratio of 0.636 and a Spearman correlation of 0.023.
item.dc:creator: Ningyuan Deng, Jinyuan Wang, Qi Li, Jia Zhang, Yi Yang

item.title: TaiJi: State-Conditional Adaptive Combination of Machine-Learning and Physics-Based Global Weather Forecasts
item.description: arXiv:2609.31972v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Data-driven machine-learning weather models now rival, and in some respects surpass, operational numerical weather prediction (NWP), yet no single model dominates across variables, pressure levels, lead times, or regions, and the marginal returns from developing ever-larger individual models are diminishing. We present TaiJi (after the Chinese concept of yin-yang harmony, the complementarity of opposites), a spatiotemporal adaptive ensemble framework that recasts optimal model-weight combination as a learned prediction problem: a lightweight convolutional neural network, conditioned on the recent atmospheric state, predicts at every grid point and lead time a set of affine combination weights and an additive residual for the constituent forecasts. The combiner is trained end-to-end over Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, FuXi, IFS-HRES, and the IFS-ENS ensemble mean, an explicitly hybrid set of ML and NWP constituents, on two consumer-grade RTX 4090 GPUs in about 8 hours, at least an order of magnitude below the training cost of any of its ML constituents. Under the WeatherBench 2 protocol (2020 test year), TaiJi outperforms the strongest baseline in nearly every combination of the eight core variables, lead times of up to 10 days and two skill metrics (RMSE and ACC), and this advantage extends to heavy-precipitation extremes. We further show that the learned weights vary coherently with latitude, season and lead time rather than following a single fixed rule. TaiJi thus offers a computationally inexpensive route to improving global forecast skill that builds on, rather than replaces, the substantial investment already made in existing forecast models.
item.dc:creator: Jiale Wang, Yining Li, Guihua Wang

item.title: Synchronization Reveals Market Structure That Classical Randomness Tests Cannot Detect
item.description: arXiv:2610.11028v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Synchronization among coupled oscillators -- from neurons to power grids -- is a universal signature of collective behavior, classically measured by the Kuramoto order parameter. Applied identically across five asset classes and 61 financial instruments, a Kuramoto-style cross-timeframe coherence measure detects structure that a calibrated, heteroskedasticity-robust variance-ratio test of the random-walk hypothesis does not: the two diagnostics are statistically independent even on the same price windows. Here we explain why, and extract the physics behind it. The four-state regime alphabet underlying the measure is a Z4 clock model whose exact factorization into two Ising sectors is precisely the order parameter's decomposition into a direction channel and a volatility channel, and the sign-flip symmetry of returns acts on the regime circle as a reflection, yielding a parity selection rule: the direction channel is provably independent of the variance ratio and of every statistic built from squared returns -- confirmed by controlled simulation on processes with and without genuine persistence. Boltzmann inversion of the regime statistics then yields effective couplings between adjacent timescales, benchmarked against matched random-walk, GARCH, and fractional-Gaussian-noise nulls: the direction sector's coupling never exceeds its random-walk null in a single instrument, and its deficit independently re-measures the panel's Hurst exponent, while the volatility sector's coupling exceeds every null in every instrument and survives across scale separations where GARCH cannot -- a volatility cascade. A closed-form mean-field analysis places markets deep below the synchronization transition, with all genuine cross-scale structure confined to the even, volatility sector.
item.dc:creator: Nam H. Le

item.title: Bayesian Optimization under Uncertainty for Training a Scale Parameter in Stochastic Models
item.description: arXiv:2510.06439v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hyperparameter tuning is a challenging problem especially when the system itself involves uncertainty. Due to noisy function evaluations, optimization under uncertainty can be computationally expensive. In this paper, we present a novel Bayesian optimization framework tailored for hyperparameter tuning under uncertainty, with a focus on optimizing a scale- or precision-type parameter in stochastic models. The proposed method employs a statistical surrogate for the underlying random variable, enabling analytical evaluation of the expectation operator. Moreover, we derive a closed-form expression for the optimizer of the random acquisition function, which significantly reduces computational cost per iteration. Numerical experiments demonstrate substantial gains in optimization efficiency: about 40-fold reduction in data usage relative to a Monte Carlo-based one-dimensional optimization scheme, and an order of magnitude improvement relative to a Gaussian process-based Bayesian optimization baseline.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: ASCE-ASME J. Risk Uncertainty Eng. Syst., Part A: Civ. Eng. 12(4): 04026050 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Akash Yadav, Ruda Zhang

item.title: From Clicks to Intent: Cross-Platform Session Embeddings with LLM-Distilled Taxonomy for Financial Services Recommendations
item.description: arXiv:2606.26277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sequential user behavior modeling is widely adopted in industrial recommender systems; however, significant gaps remain in financial services, where pre-login web interactions and authenticated in-app experiences differ drastically. Specifically, pre-login web users typically explore new products, whereas logged-in app users focus on account servicing. Due to the challenge of cross-channel entity resolution (e.g., matching anonymous web sessions to authenticated mobile accounts), web-based intent signals remain underutilized for post-authentication personalization. Existing methods for capturing web-based intent are often ad-hoc and narrow, lacking the flexibility to support both quantitative downstream recommendations and qualitative understanding at scale. In this work, we propose a scalable and dual-purpose intent prediction framework for web-based interactions and demonstrate its applicability for personalization. Our approach transforms raw web clickstreams into two outputs: a self-supervised Transformer encodes multi-modal clickstreams into a compact session embedding, while an LLM-based taxonomy generation and distillation pipeline produces interpretable intent labels. Our system demonstrates that self-supervised clickstream representations combined with LLM-distilled taxonomies can jointly serve quantitative tasks and qualitative understanding in production: on the mobile homepage tile ranking task, the session embedding improves macro Recall@1 by 1.88% and reduces Log Loss by 13.38% over production baselines. On the user conversion prediction task, the embedding outperforms the LLM labels by 4.3% on micro F1, while the distillation layer delivers interpretable labels at ultra-low latency with only a 7% performance drop.
item.dc:creator: Dianjing Fan, Yao Li, Kyaw Hpone Myint, Dwipam Katariya, Alexandre G. R. Day, Pranab Mohanty, Giri Iyengar

item.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
item.description: arXiv:2607.03698v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^\zeta$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are connected rather than by how many are active, with the current scaling approximately as \(N^{2.3}\) while the number of active junctions grows only linearly. Contrary to the expectation that junction heterogeneity strengthens the nonlinear response, homogeneous junctions in a well-connected network produce the most abrupt and reproducible turn-on. Thus, each structural parameter acts as a distinct control knob. The mean junction characteristics set the threshold, junction uniformity sets the switching sharpness, and network density and voids set the connectivity and current. These relationships provide design rules for tailoring nanonecklace networks to a desired conduction behavior through synthesis and fabrication.
item.dc:creator: Obed Issakah, Srivathsan Badrinarayanan, Ravi F. Saraf, Janghoon Ock

item.title: A Geometrically Parameterized Quasi-Stationary 3D Model for High-Frequency Induction Tube Welding
item.description: arXiv:2609.11250v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A three-dimensional multiphysics finite element model for the simulation of high-frequency induction welding of tubes is presented. The model couples a time-harmonic $h-\phi$ formulation with a stabilized quasi-stationary advection-diffusion heat transport equation, enabling accurate prediction of electromagnetic and thermal fields under industrial operating conditions. The model incorporates parameterized geometry generation and semi-automated, physics-tailored mesh construction and is implemented using the open-source tools GetDP and Gmsh. Validation against measurements from a commercial induction welding line for AISI 304 stainless steel tubes demonstrates good agreement with operating data. The validated model is subsequently applied to investigate the influence of impeder material by comparing a conventional FeNiZnV ferrite with the soft magnetic composite Ferrotron 559H for the induction welding of AISI 304 stainless steel tubes.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Ivanov, John Inge Asperheim, Bj{\o}rnar Grande, Prerana Das

item.title: Modal Integrators for Isogeometric Stabilization of Outliers
item.description: arXiv:2609.25087v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: High-order isogeometric discretizations produce a small number of non-physical outlier modes at the top of the discrete spectrum. These modes can pollute the numerical solution in wave propagation and structural dynamics. Most existing remedies modify the spatial discretization through outlier-free bases, mass lumping, subspace projection, and related constructions. We introduce MIISO (Modal Integrators for Isogeometric Stabilization of Outliers), a family of exponential Rosenbrock-Krylov methods of orders two through six that suppress the outliers in the time integrator and leave the spatial discretization unchanged. We construct a non-holomorphic amplification map by blending a Pad\'e approximation that preserves physical oscillatory modes with a Pade approximation that damps high frequencies, with the blend placed at the known spectral location of the outliers. For orders three and higher the damping approximant is repaired so that the method is unconditionally A-stable. Physical modes receive no numerical dissipation and the outliers are driven to zero. The outlier handling and the method steps are fully matrix-free, and the method extends to nonlinear problems. Numerical experiments recover the predicted orders, match spatial outlier removal without changing the discretization, show lower cost than generalized-alpha at matched accuracy and in scaling, and demonstrate the method on nonlinear and three-dimensional problems.
item.dc:creator: Sreeram Shankar

item.title: CataOPD: Catalytic On-Policy Distillation for Large Language Model Reasoning
item.description: arXiv:2609.29518v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD) are two representative paradigms for improving large language model reasoning. However, when no correct trajectory is sampled, RL lacks a positive correctness signal, while OPD remains constrained by the reasoning trajectories reachable under the student's on-policy distribution. Therefore, we propose CataOPD, where the teacher acts as a catalyst rather than a target, expanding reachability while internalizing verified student-produced trajectories into a catalyst-free policy. Self-Rescue Routing uses empirically all-failed groups as routing signals rather than teacher-intervention triggers, first seeking correct trajectories through additional on-policy self-sampling. For problems unresolved after self-rescue, Catalytic-Guided Self-Resolution uses catalytic guidance to elicit a verified student-produced trajectory in the guided student distribution. Barrier-Weighted Internalization weights tokens by guided-to-unguided log-probability gaps, focusing updates on decisive tokens difficult without guidance. Experimental results show that CataOPD outperforms current baselines, extends independent student reasoning to still-unrecovered problems, and improves out-of-distribution generalization under catalyst-free inference. Our project is available at https://github.com/QwenQKing/CataOPD.
item.dc:creator: Wenjin Liu, Chenxi Wang, Jiapu Wang, Zhe Cui, Anh Tuan Luu, Haoran Luo

item.title: When Does Interference Help Learning? Kernel Geometry as a Pre-Experimental Test for Photonic Reservoir Computing
item.description: arXiv:2610.11360v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multi-photon interference is the resource most native to photonic quantum machine learning, yet experiments on photonic reservoirs have reported advantages, null results, and train-only effects. These outcomes cannot be compared: each measures task-dependent accuracy on different tasks and platforms. Here we resolve the question task-independently through the kernel geometry of boson-sampling feature maps. Interference redistributes feature variance across roughly twice as many effective dimensions as distinguishable-particle statistics, generating a large geometric separation between the corresponding kernels. The separation grows superlinearly with indistinguishability, is linear in Hong--Ou--Mandel visibility at small visibility for two to four photons, and retains approximately 80% of its magnitude at the source quality of current quantum processors. Under experimental sampling budgets the separation is learnable on adversarially constructed tasks (accuracy advantage +0.22 plus or minus 0.05) and an order of magnitude smaller on natural tasks, gated by kernel--task alignment. The results reconcile the existing experimental record and supply a pre-experimental protocol: kernel geometry establishes that an interference-specific learning resource exists, and task alignment determines whether a given task can access it; both are computable before committing significant hardware resources.
item.dc:creator: Oishik Kar, Aswath Babu H
